xBRIEFInfo.description: Bound implementation scope for GitHub issue #4005 after the accepted design-critique synthesis.

plan.title: security: gate destination-visible empty-op Shell mutations under active UAT

narratives.Description: Close the surviving #4005 active-UAT authorization residual without reopening the already-landed shell-host catalog fix or growing another executable-name denylist.
narratives.Origin: Issue #4005 plus accepted synthesis comment 5516048869 and verified-claims table 5516040757.
narratives.Overview: The accepted design critique refutes the issue body's original bundled remedy. HIGH 1 is already satisfied by the shared SHELL_TOOL_NAMES/isShellTool path. The remaining defect is narrower: a Shell command can visibly name a protected destination yet return no authorization operation, leaving the existing active-UAT `unknown` deny branch unreachable. Exact positional `zip` writes reproduced this for `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft-directive-disable`, and `.deft/approved-scope/**`.
narratives.Contract: Add one bounded producer for the existing `unknown` authorization operation. It applies only when a protected destination is recoverable from a supported mutation shape and no stronger operation already classifies the command. The resulting `unknown` operation remains allowed when UAT is inactive and denied when UAT is active. Ordinary status, read-only protected-path access, print-only interpreter commands, and commands whose protected path is an input rather than a destination remain unclassified. The denial message must name a viable recovery: use a classifiable form or explicitly suspend UAT after human review.
narratives.ProtectedDestinations: Immediate authority effects: `.deft/authz/**` and `.deft-directive-disable` / `.no-deft-directive`. Defense in depth: `.deft/approved-scope/**`; same-change creation or rewrite is still rejected by merge-base provenance and is not claimed as immediate self-authorization.
narratives.Acceptance: 1. Exact positional `zip` writes to an authz grant, each kill-switch basename, and approved-scope produce `unknown` when no existing stronger op applies and deny under active UAT. 2. The same commands remain allowed by the Wave 1 authz evaluator when UAT is inactive. 3. `git status`, `cat .deft/authz/state.json`, `echo ok`, print-only interpreter commands, and an archive command that reads a protected file into an ordinary destination remain unclassified/allowed. 4. Existing generic destination flags continue to classify as `settings`, not `unknown`. 5. Approved-scope coverage is described and tested as defense in depth, not immediate authority. 6. Focused classifier and dispatcher/evaluator regression suites pass, followed by the repository merge gate. 7. The required pre-PR `task prd:render` refresh is retained so PRD.md names the canonical xBRIEF source directly and regenerates without further drift.
narratives.OutOfScope: Do not change the landed shell-host catalog behavior; do not add the issue body's 30 executable names as the enforcement mechanism; do not deny every empty Shell classification; do not claim total Shell parsing or expand the unrelated product path-write fence; do not claim same-change approved-scope files self-authorize.
narratives.FalsePositiveBudget: The fallback is limited to supported mutation forms with a recoverable literal protected destination. Mere mention of a protected path, read-only access, ordinary status commands, and print-only code are negative controls. Ambiguous commands outside that boundary stay on the existing fail-open path; broadening the boundary requires a separate measured change.
narratives.ImplementationSurfaces: Primary code: packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts and the active-UAT evaluator/dispatcher path. Coverage: packages/core/src/authz/classify.test.ts and packages/core/src/authz/incident-regression.test.ts, with evaluator message assertions where needed. Release note: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]. Generated pre-PR export: PRD.md, retained at the operator's direction after `task prd:render` refreshed its canonical xBRIEF source banner and footer.

items.title: Implement a bounded protected-destination fallback that emits the existing unknown op
Add exact positive and ordinary/read-only negative classifier and active-UAT tests
Keep recovery text accurate and add a brief Unreleased note
Retain the required pre-PR PRD render refresh in the approved scope

acceptance.derived_reason: The operator requested implementation by issue number; the accepted synthesis supplies behavioral clauses but no literal shell acceptance command.

clauses.text: Exact positional zip writes to each retained protected destination produce a gated operation and deny under active UAT.
Ordinary status, protected-path reads, print-only interpreter commands, and protected inputs with ordinary destinations remain unclassified.
The fallback reaches the existing unknown deny arm only under active UAT and provides accurate recovery guidance.
HIGH 1, executable-name enumeration, blanket empty-op denial, and immediate approved-scope authority claims remain out of scope.
The generated PRD names xbrief/specification.xbrief.json as its canonical source and a repeat render produces no further drift.

intended_placement.cohesion_exemption: The existing authz classifier and its focused/incident regression suites are the canonical homes for this narrow producer and its boundary tests; extracting a separate module would fragment one classifier rule without reducing those files materially. CHANGELOG.md is an append-only chronological release log, and this slice adds one [Unreleased] entry only. PRD.md is the existing generated specification export that the mandatory pre-PR render refreshed; the operator explicitly retained that deterministic output in this scope.
